text: Wikipedia's 'Signs of AI writing' guide says LLMs struggle to keep a neutral tone and produce advertisement-like or travel-guide prose even when prompted for an encyclopedic style, both in new text and in rewrites. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23)

The typical failure pattern is on cultural or geographic topics: the text keeps reminding the reader of a subject's importance using flowery description ('nestled within the breathtaking region', 'rich cultural heritage'), which asserts significance without a sourced fact. (low confidence)

Instruction-tuned Llama models overuse specific words relative to base models (e.g. 'nuanced' +8,342%, 'firstly' +4,794%), and a 400-person rating experiment found a significant preference (52.4% vs 47.6%, p<0.01) for high-overuse variants, linking lexical tics to learning from human feedback; this is Llama-only, English scientific text, and the listed words are academic, not brochure vocabulary. (low confidence)

The Wikipedia watch-word list for promotional register includes: boasts a, vibrant, rich (figurative), profound, enhancing, showcasing, exemplifies, commitment to, natural beauty, nestled, in the heart of, groundbreaking, renowned, featuring, diverse array. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23)

Word tells are weak evidence: the Wikipedia guide itself says not all promotional writing is AI-generated, and a legal-tech commentator notes they used 'delve' before LLMs existed, so single-word detection is insufficient proof. (medium confidence)

Wikipedia's guide reports older models such as GPT-4 write more blatantly positive text, while newer models are more subtly positive and avoid obvious superlatives like 'the best', so a superlative-only filter under-detects newer output. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23)
